title: Sage Butter Crescent Rolls
changes_from_base: Rich egg dough flavoured with sage, rolled into 18 butter-brushed crescents.
summary: Rich, buttery crescent rolls flecked with sage, ideal alongside a roast.
equipment: large bowl or stand mixer with dough hook
cling film or a clean tea towel
two baking trays lined with baking paper

steps.title: Dough
steps.text: Mix and knead all the dough ingredients for 8-10 min, until soft and smooth but not sticky.

steps.title: Rise
steps.text: Cover and leave about 1 1/2 h, until doubled.

steps.title: Cut
steps.text: Divide the dough in half. Roll one half into a 22 cm circle and cut it like a cake into 9 long triangles.

steps.title: Roll up
steps.text: Starting from the wide end, roll each triangle towards its point and set it point side down on a tray, bending the ends into a gentle curve. Brush with some of the melted butter, then repeat with the second half.

steps.title: Prove
steps.text: Cover loosely and leave 25-35 min, until puffy but not doubled. Heat the oven to 180 °C (160 °C fan).

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake about 18-20 min, until golden; the thickest part reads 88-90 °C. Brush with the rest of the butter and serve warm.

tips: Stretch each triangle gently before rolling for more layers.
Tuck the point underneath so the crescents do not unroll.
Use 2 tsp dried sage if fresh is not available.
storage: Keep cooled rolls in an airtight bag at room temperature for up to 2 days. Rewarm at 180 °C for 5 min; freeze for up to 1 month. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
